chunks: Protect them from the evil deeds; and whoever You preserve from the evil deeds on that Day, then You have had mercy on him, and that is the great triumph.

key_terms.يَوْمَئِذٍ: On that Day (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of being preserved from evil deeds in relation to divine mercy?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often recited in supplications like those of Imam Ali (AS) to seek protection from the consequences of sins, emphasizing that divine mercy is the true measure of success. It highlights the concept that avoiding evil is not merely avoidance of punishment but an active attainment of 'Al-Fawz al-Azeem' (the Great Triumph), linking human agency with divine grace.
